items.title: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, its production inference framework
items.summary: DeepSeek released the in-house inference stack it uses to serve DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, so teams self-hosting its models can run the same high-throughput, low-latency serving code.

reception.summary: Repliers mostly cheered the open release; one asked for end-to-end throughput on Ascend NPUs and nobody reported running it yet.

items.title: Mistral releases Voxtral 3 transcription and speech models
items.summary: Mistral shipped Voxtral 3 Transcribe and Speech models behind a new voice agents API, giving developers one vendor for speech in, speech out and the agent loop.

doubt.pushback: Repliers asked whether weights will be on Hugging Face and one found the generated voice still robotic.

reception.summary: Mostly positive; questions about turn-taking, interruption handling and open weights, plus one complaint that the voice sounds robotic.

video.shows: An unedited live conversation between two people and a Voxtral 3 voice agent, with real-time transcription and speaker labels on screen.
video.why: A continuous live demo showing real turn-taking, interruptions and tool calls with no cuts.
learn: Voxtral 3 runs transcription and turn detection, Mistral Large reasoning, and Voxtral speech as three parallel streams
The agent stops mid-sentence when interrupted and switches between English, French and German
It can run a web search tool call mid-conversation
video.audience: Developers building voice agents or speech-to-speech products.

items.title: ElevenLabs launches Eleven Realtime speech-to-speech models
items.summary: ElevenLabs released speech-to-speech models for voice agents that it says start speaking in about half a second while still answering spoken reasoning questions correctly (98.8% on Big Bench Audio, self-reported).

reception.summary: Positive; repliers asked about pricing and language coverage, and nobody reported testing it yet.

video.shows: An animated launch video for the Eleven Realtime Mini and Max speech-to-speech models, using abstract graphics and simulated voice exchanges.
video.why: A polished concept montage with no real interface or live output.
learn: Eleven Realtime ships two speech-to-speech models: Mini for fast conversation and Max for complex tasks and tool calling
It claims 400 to 800 ms latency, with turn-taking and interruption handled natively
video.audience: Product leads wanting a high-level overview.

items.title: Anthropic: Claude-designed protein binders against scorpion neurotoxins
items.summary: Anthropic reports Claude designed protein binders against scorpion toxins; of 211 designs tested in the lab, 17 bound their target. An early research step toward cheaper antivenom, not a treatment.

doubt.pushback: Repliers point out binding in a lab assay is far from neutralizing venom in cells or animals, which the post does not yet show.

reception.summary: Positive with caution; scientists noted the gap between binding and a working antivenom. One reply tried to direct AI summarizers and was ignored.

items.title: Meta publishes the Muse Glimmer 30B open-weight technical report
items.summary: Meta detailed Muse Glimmer, a 30B open-weight agentic model meant to run on a Mac or a single consumer GPU at 4-bit, and says it leads similar-size open models on tool use.

reception.summary: Positive; one replier reported about 33 tokens per second on an M5 Max, others pointed to the Hugging Face weights.

items.title: Inception releases Mercury 3 diffusion LLM at over 1,000 tokens per second
items.summary: Inception's Mercury 3 is a diffusion language model with a 1M-token context that it says beats GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 on standard benchmarks while generating over 1,000 tokens per second, via an OpenAI-compatible API.

doubt.pushback: The benchmark wins are self-reported; repliers say to wait for independent leaderboards before trusting the Luna and Haiku comparison.

reception.summary: Many generic congratulations; serious repliers asked about multi-file edits and editor support, and quote posts note people questioning the value of a fast Luna-level model.

video.shows: A developer introduces Mercury 3, then a side-by-side terminal recording of a coding agent building six arcade games with Mercury 3 and with Claude Sonnet 5.5, ending in a cost and latency chart (video post: https://x.com/_inception_ai/status/2112588104955773059).
video.why: A working head-to-head agent run with real output and cost and time numbers.
learn: Mercury 3 is a diffusion LLM claiming over 1,000 tokens per second
In the demo it built six games in under 5 minutes for about $0.10, versus over 50 minutes and nearly $5 for Sonnet 5.5
The speed suits agent workflows that fan out many sub-agents and tool calls
video.audience: Engineers building coding agents or high-throughput LLM apps.

items.title: fal and Black Forest Labs release FLUX 3 Max video model
items.summary: fal Research post-trained FLUX 3 Max with Black Forest Labs: a 10-second 720p video in about 12 seconds, tied for first on Artificial Analysis image-to-video quality.

doubt.pushback: It is built on an open-weight base but the post-trained weights are not released, and repliers say it lacks reference-video input.

reception.summary: Speed impressed people; complaints about no weights and no reference input. One quote poster generated a 15-second clip in 36 seconds.

items.title: OpenAI reports big gains on COBOL, Fortran and Visual Basic coding
items.summary: OpenAI says its latest models build and migrate software in low-resource languages far better: 87.4% average on its MultiLangBench (released on GitHub) and up to 97.9% on a COBOL migration eval with hidden byte-parity tests.

doubt.pushback: Repliers say passing OpenAI's own migration eval does not prove behavioral equivalence on real legacy systems with undocumented rules.

reception.summary: Interest from people who maintain legacy code, many jokes, and recurring skepticism that the hard part is preserving undocumented behavior.

items.title: Anthropic launches OSS Scanner, free vulnerability scans for critical open source
items.summary: Maintainers of critical open-source projects can opt in to periodic vulnerability scans by Anthropic's strongest models, with a proof-of-concept and, where possible, a patch for each finding.

doubt.pushback: The 88% hit rate on high and critical findings comes from Anthropic grading its own scanner.

reception.summary: Strongly positive; maintainers valued patches over bare reports and asked whether smaller projects can join.

items.title: Vals AI: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash beats GPT 6 Sol on a multi-step offensive cyber task
items.summary: Vals AI says the open-weight DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 outscored GPT 6 Sol on its unreleased simulated corporate network attack benchmark, a signal of cyber risk from cheap open models.

doubt.pushback: Vals's own public CyberBench still ranks GPT 6 Sol above Flash (77.98% vs 73.69%), and repliers say the comparison ran models in uneven access modes.

reception.summary: Alarm and interest, plus pointed questions on harness, run counts and fairness of the Opus 5.5 setup; full eval not yet published.

items.title: Perplexity Computer can now run fully local on a Mac
items.summary: Perplexity's Computer agent and its model can now run entirely on a Mac, working with local apps and files without sending data to the cloud.

items.title: Devin Fusion scores 68 on Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index
items.summary: Cognition's Devin Fusion, pairing Opus 5.5 with GPT-6 Luna, scored 68 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index at 31% lower cost per task than Claude Code with Opus 5.5.

items.title: Notion AI adds stronger agents, bring-your-own-key and a better MCP server
items.summary: Notion upgraded its agents, added a cheaper Auto model mode, bring-your-own AI keys and an improved Notion MCP server.

items.title: ChatGPT team tasks automate recurring engineering updates
items.summary: Teams can schedule recurring engineering work in ChatGPT, such as a weekly shipped-and-blocked report, and teammates can review and steer the next run.

items.title: Zed benchmarks 25 approaches to MCP tool search
items.summary: Zed tested 25 MCP tool search methods on 150 queries over 536 tools and chose weighted BM25, which needs no model or API calls.

items.title: Sakana AI releases QD-Rec, quality-diversity recommendations for decisions
items.summary: Sakana's QD-Rec evolves a diverse set of proposals to support decisions like which papers to read or companies to evaluate, with paper and code.

items.title: AllenAI releases FairStress, a fairness benchmark beyond final answers
items.summary: FairStress tests how easily a model flips a well-supported decision based on demographics and how it explains the choice.

items.title: Aleph Alpha: one space in a multiple-choice prompt changes what the eval measures
items.summary: Aleph Alpha shows that moving one space in a multiple-choice eval shifts the correct answer's probability by orders of magnitude while accuracy barely moves.

items.title: MiniCPM-V 4.7 35B runs at 20 tokens per second on an iPhone
items.summary: OpenBMB reports 20.51 tokens per second for its 35B-A3B multimodal MoE on an iPhone 18 Pro Max, 6x faster than its unoptimized expert-loading baseline.

items.title: Hermes agent can launch Cua Spaces sandboxes
items.summary: Hermes can now create a Cua Space on a Mac, Windows or Linux machine for a task, work there, then delete it, and teammates can join the same Space.

items.title: Prime Intellect releases prime-rl v0.10.0 and verifiers v0.4.0
items.summary: prime-rl now defaults to Prime Intellect's IPO algorithm, tuned for async RL stability, with speedups and new model support.

items.title: SGLang adds Low-Latency Mode for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
items.summary: SGLang's new mode raises P90 per-user token speed up to 1.38x on NVIDIA GB300 and 1.56x on AMD MI355X in SemiAnalysis's AgentX trace replay.

items.title: PyTorch 2.15 speeds up Mac inference with new Metal kernels
items.summary: Hugging Face's PyTorch team replaced MPSGraph paths with Metal kernels upstream; MoE decoding on Mac is 5 to 6.5x faster.

items.title: TRL v1.16 adds AWS Trainium fine-tuning
items.summary: TRL can now fine-tune language and vision-language models on AWS Trainium through TorchNeuron, with up to 2x faster training on Trainium2.

items.title: Vals AI releases ClaimBench for decision models
items.summary: ClaimBench checks whether a model can tell if a 10-K excerpt supports, contradicts or ignores a financial claim; 15 models on 1,960 claims.

items.title: Artificial Analysis launches HealthBench leaderboards
items.summary: Artificial Analysis now runs independent leaderboards for OpenAI's HealthBench and HealthBench Professional health-conversation benchmarks.

items.title: Ant Group's inclusionAI releases Ming-3.0 TTS, audio and ASR models
items.summary: The Ming-3.0 speech family covers text-to-speech, audio understanding and speech recognition for calls and voice search.

items.title: Bria Fibo 2.0 open-weight image editing model lands on fal
items.summary: Bria's Fibo 2.0, trained only on licensed data, does multi-image editing and text-to-image and tops Artificial Analysis among open-weight editing models.

items.title: Krea 3 Ultra enters top five in Arena image edit leaderboards
items.summary: Krea 3 Ultra placed fourth in Multi-Image Edit (1435 points) and fifth by lab in Single-Image Edit on Arena.

items.title: Meta details goodput engineering on its Prometheus supercluster
items.summary: Meta explains how it keeps a run across hundreds of thousands of GPUs from being slowed by single underperforming hosts.

items.title: Paper: open questions and best practices for agent evaluation
items.summary: Princeton researchers compile best practices and open problems for evaluating AI agents, aimed at people entering the field.

items.title: Meta ProPerAgent harness raises proactive agent accuracy to 38%
items.summary: A Meta harness for proactive agents lifts accuracy from at most 15% with standard memory to 38% without changing model weights.

items.title: Kiro's CORVUS cuts coding agent input tokens 9 to 50%
items.summary: CORVUS keeps one live copy of each file in context instead of stale duplicates, cutting input tokens 9 to 50% with the same pass rates.

items.title: OpenVLHarness: visual agentic tool use with multimodal memory
items.summary: A new benchmark and harness for real-world visual agent tool use with multimodal memory.

items.title: Rapid-MLX 0.16.5 runs full DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on a 256GB Mac
items.summary: Rapid-MLX ships an MLX build of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 with no experts removed, runnable on a 256GB Apple Silicon Mac.

items.title: Factory Droids accept Linear issue delegations
items.summary: Delegating a Linear issue to Factory now starts a Droid working on it.

items.title: Hamel Husain: how to choose and tune decision models for evals
items.summary: A guide to picking a decision model for an eval task, tuning its threshold rather than using 0.5, and reading its scores.

items.title: CoreWeave previews GPU sandboxes for RL training
items.summary: CoreWeave Sandboxes now offer GPU sandboxes in preview, billed hourly, isolating failures across thousands of RL sandboxes per step.

saved_rejected.reason: Personal Google TV launcher built with an AI coding tool; no new AI capability.
